The Nasdaq's Worst Week Since 2020. Now What?

2026-11-21

Subscribe for one money story a week

About this video

The Nasdaq Composite fell 10.0% in the week to Nov 20, 2026, its worst week since March 2020. The S&P 500 fell 8.6%, its worst week since April 2025, and closed at 6,910.39: 11.6% below its Oct 6 record, which makes it a correction. We go through the week day by day, why stocks fell (bond yields over 5%, 4.1% inflation, the Fed's September hike, the tech unwind, a fear index at 37), where the money went (gold -9.5%, bitcoin -13.8%, Treasuries up), and every S&P 500 correction since 1950: 26 of them, 15 stopped before a bear market, and a year after first hitting -10% the index was higher 18 of 26 times (median +14%). 0:00 Intro: the worst week since 2020 0:47 The week, day by day 1:31 What a correction is 2:05 Why stocks fell 3:03 Where the money went 3:45 Every correction since 1950 4:12 How long corrections last 4:39 One year later 5:17 Recent corrections 6:01 Weeks this bad 6:29 What to watch next week 6:53 What it means for you 7:28 Recap Sources: Yahoo Finance daily closes for the S&P 500 (^GSPC), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC), Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI), Cboe VIX (^VIX), COMEX gold futures (GC=F), bitcoin (BTC-USD) and the U.S. dollar index (DX-Y.NYB), through Nov 20, 2026. FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis): DGS10, DFEDTARU/DFEDTARL, CPIAUCSL, MORTGAGE30US (Freddie Mac).
